checks.message: RDS storage encryption not enabled
checks.context: Unencrypted RDS snapshots can be shared or copied to another account, exposing your entire database. Encryption cannot be enabled after creation — you'd need to snapshot, restore, and migrate.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled
checks.context: Without this, a single `rds delete-db-instance` command — accidental or malicious — permanently destroys your database. This is a one-line safeguard that has saved countless production databases.

checks.message: RDS instance set to publicly accessible
checks.context: A publicly accessible database is reachable from the entire internet. Automated scanners will find it and attempt brute-force logins within hours. Databases should only be reachable from within your VPC.

checks.message: Public accessibility not explicitly disabled. RDS may default to publicly accessible
checks.context: Depending on VPC and subnet group configuration, RDS instances can default to publicly accessible. Always explicitly set --no-publicly-accessible to ensure the database is not reachable from the internet.

checks.message: Backup retention period not specified
checks.context: The default backup retention is 1 day. For production databases, set this to at least 7 days to allow recovery from ransomware or accidental data corruption that isn't immediately noticed.

checks.message: CloudWatch log exports not configured
checks.context: Without log exports, you have no visibility into slow queries, errors, or suspicious login attempts. Log types vary by engine: MySQL/MariaDB (audit, error, general, slowquery), PostgreSQL (postgresql, upgrade), Oracle (alert, audit, listener, trace), SQL Server (agent, error).

checks.message: IAM database authentication not enabled
checks.context: IAM authentication lets applications connect to MySQL and PostgreSQL using short-lived IAM tokens instead of static database passwords. This eliminates a class of credential leak: no database password to rotate, store, or accidentally commit. Supported on MySQL 5.6.34+, PostgreSQL 9.5.15+, and Aurora.

checks.message: Making RDS instance publicly accessible
checks.context: You are about to expose a database directly to the internet. If this is for debugging, use an SSH tunnel or SSM port forwarding instead — then revert this change immediately after.

checks.message: Disabling deletion protection on RDS instance
checks.context: Removing deletion protection makes the database vulnerable to accidental or malicious deletion. Only disable this immediately before a planned deletion, then re-enable it if the deletion is cancelled.

checks.message: Aurora cluster storage encryption not enabled
checks.context: Unencrypted Aurora clusters expose all data at rest. Encryption must be set at creation time and cannot be added later without creating a new cluster.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled on Aurora cluster
checks.context: Without deletion protection, the entire cluster and all its instances can be deleted with a single command. Enable this to prevent accidental or malicious destruction of your database.

checks.message: Backup retention period not specified
checks.context: Default retention is 1 day. Set to at least 7 days for production workloads to allow recovery from data corruption or ransomware that isn't immediately detected.

checks.message: No final snapshot specified: database will be deleted without a backup
checks.context: Without --final-db-snapshot-identifier, the database is deleted without a backup. Always take a final snapshot unless you are 100% certain the data is no longer needed.

checks.message: Explicitly skipping final snapshot. All data will be permanently lost
checks.context: With --skip-final-snapshot, no backup is taken before deletion. If you need this data later, it is gone forever.

checks.message: Restoring RDS instance as publicly accessible
checks.context: Restored instances should default to private. Exposing a restored database to the internet is rarely intentional and creates immediate risk.

checks.message: Public accessibility not explicitly disabled on restored instance
checks.context: Restored RDS instances can inherit public accessibility from the snapshot or default to publicly accessible depending on the subnet group. Always explicitly set --no-publicly-accessible.

checks.message: Verify snapshot is not shared publicly after creation
checks.context: RDS snapshots shared with 'all' are accessible to any AWS account. After creation, check with `rds describe-db-snapshot-attributes` to confirm the snapshot is private.

checks.message: Verify audit logging parameters are enabled in the parameter group
checks.context: For Aurora MySQL, set server_audit_logging=ON and server_audit_events to include CONNECT and QUERY_DCL. For Aurora PostgreSQL, enable pgaudit. Without audit logging, you have no record of who ran what queries.

checks.message: Manual failover causes a brief outage — notify your team first
checks.context: Aurora failover typically takes 30-120 seconds. Applications that don't handle connection drops gracefully will error during this window. Ensure your app uses the cluster endpoint (not instance endpoint) and has retry logic.

checks.message: Public accessibility not explicitly disabled on restored cluster
checks.context: Restored clusters can default to publicly accessible depending on subnet group configuration. Always explicitly set --no-publicly-accessible to prevent internet exposure.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled on restored cluster
checks.context: Restored clusters do not inherit deletion protection from the snapshot. Explicitly enable it to prevent accidental deletion.

checks.message: Disabling deletion protection on Aurora cluster
checks.context: Only disable this immediately before a planned deletion. Leaving deletion protection off on a production cluster is an accident waiting to happen.

checks.message: Parameter changes affect all instances using this group — verify you're not weakening SSL or logging
checks.context: Disabling require_secure_transport (MySQL) or rds.force_ssl (PostgreSQL) allows unencrypted database connections. Disabling audit logging removes compliance visibility. Changes may require a reboot.

checks.message: Sharing a snapshot with 'all' makes your entire database publicly accessible
checks.context: A public RDS snapshot allows any AWS account to copy and restore your database. This exposes all data in the snapshot. Only share with specific trusted account IDs.
